title: Locators: refactor to user-facing
summary: The starter test passes but uses CSS selectors. Refactor it to getByLabel / getByRole / getByText and also assert you landed on the dashboard.
why: Locators that read like the UI (label, role, accessible name) keep working when developers rename ids or restructure markup, and they double as a basic accessibility check.
objectives: Use getByLabel for the Email and Password fields
Assert the URL with toHaveURL and the greeting with getByText(...)
hints: Priority: getByRole → getByLabel → getByPlaceholder → getByText → getByAltText/getByTitle → getByTestId → CSS/XPath (last resort).
pitfalls: CSS such as 'form button[type=submit]' breaks the day a second form appears.
Asserting only the URL: a broken greeting would slip through.
teachAlong: Cause: locators describe what a user sees.
Effect: markup refactors don't break the test.
Gate: CSS/XPath fail this task; the app is also run with planted bugs your assertions must catch.

requires.reason: Fill the fields by their visible label: page.getByLabel('Email') / page.getByLabel('Password').
Click the button by role and name: page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign in' }).
Assert where the user lands: await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard$/).

mutants.reason: after sign-in the app goes to the home page instead of the dashboard
the dashboard greets the user as 'Guest'
